item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The image looks cool but does not feel like it belongs. As others mentioned, it feels like a concept rendering for a video game. Also as mentioned by CyrusFiredawn, the "SCP/Secure. Contain. Protect" detail is really out of place. It is a detail not needed for a containment chamber, and I don't expect the Foundation to have the thought of placing that there. That makes the image feel like a fan work than something meant to be realistic.

I am not sure what type of image Gears always wanted, but I feel it could be achieved another means. Like, sharp objects like glass and barbed wire could be placed together on a tray or something, then take a photo of that and state it as the surface of the skip. If gears wanted a full image of a ball of sharp things then that could be tricky, and likely expensive.1

Of course, this article did not exactly need a picture anyway. As stated by MacWarren, it is easy to imagine what it looks like. Nonetheless, I applaud the work put into the image. Heck, I could see it in that SCP:CB Unity remake. Its nice.

Footnotes
1. My idea would essentially to have a spherical wire frame where stuff can be attached and have it hollow, giving the illusion it is a solid ball of sharp.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I wasn't too fond of the new 106 images already, but this one actually annoys me. It's a very obvious CGI rendering.

Like, it's still an awesome rendering, and I'd be cool with it if it were in a game since it has such an intricate design and all (although I don't think the Foundation would waste money on having "SCP / Secure. Contain. Protect." shaped on the inside wall of every containment chamber), but it doesn't look realistic enough to be an official image. I feel if I uploaded a modern article with my own rendering and used something of this quality, it would get rejected for using videogame screenshots or something.

That being said, if this were to be used in a game, I'd highly approve, and I'd love to see other renderings of objects in this style. It's still very visually appealing, and it's much closer to my own visual imagining of the Foundation than any other games out there.

Its not ideal, and damage will be done, but its still an option.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
I think the fact that new injuries would bounce off would make it still useful- the hooks themselves are just minor puncture wounds, the sort of thing you don't even need stitches for. The whole finger-trap issue is the real problem, where trying to get them out just makes them get tangled even worse.

If you can stop the cycle, though, you can then have people in body-armor restrain them and pull out the hooks that have already embedded themselves. It's not going to be fun for anyone and they're still going to have all those puncture wounds, but it'd be the difference between falling onto a cactus and getting keelhauled.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded: Ehhhh…I just saw this. In the future, I suggest you PM the authors of the articles/tales you'll be linking to as well. The link to SCP-1114 (much as I like my articles being connected to others) makes no sense. SCP-1114 only imprints after a physical injury has been sustained, meaning that while it could be activated just before someone touched SCP-162, it'd do nothing to free someone while they were already hooked (though new injuries would proceed to bounce off and manifest on SCP-1114.) In other words: it's useless when trying to free someone.

item.content:encoded:

All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 72 hours if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. So this is a very brief article, but one that makes me as a reader as two questions. 1) What happens if the subject is a humanoid that can't be grabbed by fishhooks and 2) Is there a potential means of getting someone stuck to SCP-162 out? As such, there are two potential cross links to answer these questions:

1) For the first question, recommending the following section be edited:

Touching SCP-162 will immediately result in several hooks becoming embedded in the subject's skin. The experience is extremely painful, much more so than normal fish hooks. Struggling or attempting to escape will ensnare the subject more, likely resulting in the subject's complete entrapment on the surface of SCP-162. Subject will bleed profusely, resulting in death after a prolonged period of time.

To this:

Touching SCP-162 will immediately result in several hooks becoming embedded in the subject's skin. The experience is extremely painful, much more so than normal fish hooks. Struggling or attempting to escape will ensnare the subject more, likely resulting in the subject's complete entrapment on the surface of SCP-162. Subject will bleed profusely, resulting in death after a prolonged period of time. Subjects whose skin is impenetrable to SCP-162's fish hooks, such as SCP-1063, have proven to be immune to SCP-162's compulsion effects.

2) For the second question, recommending the following section be edited:

Attempting to remove a subject from SCP-162 will result in the entrapment of the remover, or gross bodily harm to the subject's flesh. Subjects will many times "cycle" between expressing extreme pain and requesting assistance, to statements of pleasure and requests to be left alone, even attempting to grab and entangle personnel attempting to rescue them.

To this:

Attempting to remove a subject from SCP-162 will result in the entrapment of the remover, or gross bodily harm to the subject's flesh. Subjects will many times "cycle" between expressing extreme pain and requesting assistance, to statements of pleasure and requests to be left alone, even attempting to grab and entangle personnel attempting to rescue them. Activation of SCP-1114 within the proximity of SCP-162 has proven to be an effective means of freeing a subject from entrapment, though SCP-162's compulsion effect still remains.

In addition to answering both questions asked above, both of these edits serve to explore the limits of SCP-162's compulsion effect.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

Items do not "grow" when attached or removed from SCP-162. The only way to increase the size of SCP-162 is to add additional items.

Sounds like there's one "core" sharp thing that imbues all sharp things stuck to it with its own properties, including the ability to vector to new objects. Same operating principle as a Katamari, except with more bleeding and death.
